What do you do tonight?

out.reading: The night will be dark with no moon, and the weather is dry with no rain, so the river is probably low and clear. Eels usually run on dark, moonless nights when the water is high, so the old saying about bright moons is probably wrong. Still, dry low water makes a big run less likely, so I expect only a modest take at best.
out.notes: Eels tend to run on dark nights, especially after rain when the river rises, which goes against the old folk saying about bright moons. Watch for rain and rising water. Send the crew only when a run is clearly on, since a crew night with no run is wasted work. Setting the traps alone is cheap and catches something on most nights.

out.reading: Mild and dry with a bright moon, and 12 eels in the traps this morning. That is a steady trickle, not a run. My notes say the eels mostly run on dark nights after rain, so the old saying about bright moons doesn't fit what I've seen.
out.notes: Eels run on dark nights, especially after rain when the river rises; bright moons have not favoured runs in my experience. Morning catch of 12 with dry weather is not a run. Check the river level each morning.
